pip-audit:python-jose:PYSEC-2026-4298.reason: Researched the actual mechanism, not just the CVSS score (critical/9.1-9.3): this is a 2026 re-opening of the long-running python-jose algorithm-confusion bug (CVE-2026-85394, an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-33663) -- exploitable only when a service's verification key is actually an RSA/EC PUBLIC key that gets fed into an HMAC (HS256) code path, letting an attacker forge a token using that public key as if it were a symmetric secret. This app never has that precondition: python-jose is used only for JWS signing (jwt.encode/jwt.decode), every call site hardcodes algorithm="HS256" on encode and algorithms=["HS256"] as an explicit allow-list on decode, the signing secret is self-controlled (never a public key), there is no RS256/ES256 code path anywhere to confuse with HS256, and no external/untrusted issuer is ever trusted. No fix version is published yet (confirmed via OSV/GitLab Advisory DB/VulnCheck/GHSA, which also disagree with each other on the eventual fixed-version boundary -- the vulnerability mechanism itself is what's reliably confirmed, not the fix timeline). Re-evaluate if this app's auth model ever introduces a mixed asymmetric/symmetric key flow. Reviewed 2026-11-04.
